method: Root viewed revision002 coupled-response PNG through SSH base64. The late-mechanics PNG is byte-identical to the already viewed revision001 image. No local image processing.
visual_checks: Labels, axes, units, arm colors and intervention interval are readable.
The response plot shows the observed drop in breath inspiration volume and arterial oxygen, rise in arterial carbon dioxide, and subsequent recovery toward baseline.
Late plots show inspiratory and expiratory flow, diaphragm and rib displacement, a pressure-volume path, a sampled complete left-ventricular cycle, and pulsatile arterial pressures.
interpretation_limits: Trailing 30-second ventilation varies with how breath phases overlap the window; it is not a per-breath steady-state rate.
The linear transpulmonary pressure-volume path reflects the declared constant lung compliance; no hysteresis or regional tissue validation is implied.
Cardiovascular curves overlap because the cardiovascular operating point lacks dynamic respiratory-pressure or autonomic feedback.
The approximately 0.098 mL running maximum absolute blood-volume deviation is visible. Its monotonicity follows from the high-water definition and does not establish monotonic physical drift.
Viewing trace plots is not an anatomical or native onscreen UI qualification.
correction: The original review used the word accumulated for the blood field; that was imprecise. Source lines1253–1258 update circulation.w as max(previous, abs(current total minus0.00515f)). Revision002 labels the same unchanged data as a running maximum. It is not instantaneous drift or the sum of errors.
